doc.title: Ruth Lion interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998

title: Working for love and her cable access award
summary: She congratulated on her PACE award, she says she learned from Alfred to love work, and reflects on the arts.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: And you must really enjoy working.

I do. I learned that. I always enjoyed working. But I learned it from him because he was so in love with his work. In fact on his gravestone I had printed “Through jazz he lived the life he loved.” And I learned that from him. You don’t always feel like working. But if you love that work you’ll go ahead and do it, sick or well.
Right. It’s fortunate when you can work at what you love. Not everyone is able to do that.

Not everyone. But I think even so, maybe that’s why the arts have become so prominent today. Because everybody can have something that they enjoy, of the arts. Whether it’s painting or sculpting or music, whatever it might be, you can add that dimension to your life and enjoy your life. Because we can’t all be into one thing that is a full life.
